name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (34%) and a 4.3% free-cash-flow yield, 4.6 points ahead of the ETF since purchase; health care is one of the sectors holding up in this correction.
targets.risks: The GAAP P/E of 143 includes one-off charges, and a pipeline or patent setback would hit the earnings path.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 8.4% above), or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; it fell only 5% in a month when energy fell 11%, and it is now my only energy name, 4 points ahead of the ETF.
targets.risks: Lower oil prices from Middle East peace talks could slow Permian drilling and volumes, and net debt is 31% of market value.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 6.4% above), or management cuts its volume guidance.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 15.8, a 4.8% free-cash-flow yield and a solid balance sheet, 1.7 points ahead of the ETF; trimmed slightly to match medium conviction.
targets.risks: A recession scare or looser steel tariffs would hit steel prices, and it is my whole materials overweight.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 7.3% above), or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: The slimmer post-breakup DuPont keeps rising in a falling market (+11.7% over a month, 2% under its high) and is 25 points ahead of the ETF since purchase, with a 3.9% free-cash-flow yield.
targets.risks: Its GAAP P/E of 75 (breakup charges included) leaves little room if the re-rating stalls.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 9.7% above), or its lead over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

targets.name: Hasbro
targets.thesis: Growing (+19% revenue) and profitable (18% margin), with a 7.9% free-cash-flow yield at a P/E of 16.5; my steadiest share (25% volatility), 17% above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: It fell 6.8% this week for a reason I could not confirm, and its Q4 depends on holiday toy demand and the digital gaming segment.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 16.8% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.3% free-cash-flow yield; up 6% over a month in a falling market and 15 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: Net debt is 51% of market value and GAAP earnings are negative, so any setback in debt reduction would hurt.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 20% above), or debt reduction stalls.

targets.name: Target Corporation
targets.thesis: Q3 beat with raised full-year guidance; up 16% over a month, 2% under its high, at a P/E of 16 with a 5.3% free-cash-flow yield; it fills my staples weight and is 4 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: Part of the guidance raise came from one-off tariff refunds, and holiday sales could disappoint.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 23.6% above), or holiday sales trends reverse the raised guidance.

targets.name: Visa Inc.
targets.thesis: New: a payments network with 15% revenue growth and a 51% net margin, 2.7% under its 52-week high and 21% above its 200-day average while the index falls. It lifts my financials from 5% toward the index's 13% with a steadier share than Morgan Stanley.
targets.risks: It is priced as a quality compounder (the brief shows no P/E), so it could lag if money rotates back into tech, and US card-fee regulation is a standing risk.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Big move, kept as an overreaction: Q3 (reported November 23) was strong (revenue +28% to $1.58 billion, record net new annual recurring revenue of $419 million, guidance raised). The roughly 9% drop that day came from the $43.9 billion all-stock Zscaler deal, not the business, and the share is still 15.7% above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: The Zscaler deal dilutes existing holders and adds integration risk, and at 77% volatility the share swings with the tech selloff.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or the Zscaler integration points to sharply slower recurring-revenue growth.

targets.name: Omnicom Group
targets.thesis: Organic growth accelerated to 7.2% in Q3 as Interpublic synergies arrive; it has an 11.6% free-cash-flow yield and net cash, is at its 52-week high and up 14.8% over a month, and it is my only communication-services name in a sector where I am 5 points under the index.
targets.risks: Its GAAP margin of 2.8% reflects merger costs, and ad budgets would shrink if the selloff turns into a recession scare.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 14.3% above), or organic growth falls back below 3%.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Storage for AI data at a P/E of 23, with a 5.1% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; held into Q2 results after the close on December 1 (confirmed), against guidance of $2.025-2.175 billion in revenue.
targets.risks: The AI-hardware selloff plus any results miss could push it through its 200-day average (now 4.3% above).
targets.exit_if: Q2 revenue or guidance disappoints, or it closes more than 3% under its 200-day average.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Record fiscal Q4 on November 19 (revenue +41%, orders +53%) shows AI and networking test demand is strong; the 20% monthly fall tracks the AI-hardware selloff, not its business.
targets.risks: As an AI-hardware supplier it keeps falling with the chip complex (75% volatility, 17% under its 200-day average).
targets.exit_if: It falls more than 25% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 20 points since purchase (now 13.6), or a fiscal 2027 outlook implies growth below 10%.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth-management fees and capital markets at a P/E of 13.3, with 16% revenue growth and a 25.5% margin; level with the ETF since purchase (+0.4 points).
targets.risks: It is 14.1% under its 200-day average, just above my exit line, and a falling market cuts deal and asset-based fees.
targets.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Q3 beat with raised guidance, a 20% net margin and net cash; still 9% above its 200-day average, so the 29% monthly fall looks like the unwind of high-momentum shares, though I could not confirm a cause.
targets.risks: Revenue growth is only 5.8% at a P/E of 34.5, and an unexplained drop while health care rose could hide a company-specific problem.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase (now 17).

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
